capabilities: Import recipes from URLs, JSON-LD files, folders, and photos
Browse recipes in a visual gallery with ingredient search
Cook recipes step by step in cook mode
Build a combined, aisle-sorted shopping list from ticked ingredients
Scale recipes, track times made, and export as JSON-LD or Cooklang
extras: The optional proxy fallback sends blocked recipe URLs to the third-party service allorigins.win; the README includes a privacy section detailing all network use. AI features are pay-as-you-go via OpenRouter (photo import averages under $0.001 per recipe) and can be disabled entirely. Documentation site: recipe-vault docs at taylordugger.com.
intentEvidence: Recipe Vault is based on obsidian-recipe-grabber by @seethroughdev, which provided the original URL import foundation.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to capture recipes from the web, read them while cooking, track what you have made, or turn ingredients into a shopping list.

relations.evidence: Recipe Vault is based on obsidian-recipe-grabber by @seethroughdev, which provided the original URL import foundation.

summary: Recipe management system that imports recipes from URLs or photos, browses them in a gallery, and builds aisle-sorted shopping lists.
